name: Variable-Font Data Morph
summary: Type weight is the data: a weight wave scans a grid of numerals and the one that stays heavy is the anomaly.
look: A cool pale field of tabular numerals in a variable sans; glyph weight (200–800) encodes deviation from normal. Healthy numbers stay thin and grey-teal, the anomaly holds at black weight in coral with a halo, then swells into a hero number.

components.name: Type grid
components.role: 12 columns of two-digit numerals in a 200–800 variable sans, tabular figures

components.name: Weight wave
components.role: moving front driving font-weight by distance: the visual form of the scan

components.name: Anomaly glyph
components.role: the one numeral that stays at 800, coral, with a halo ring

components.name: Axis legend
components.role: 'wght = deviation' with sample glyphs from 200 to 800

components.name: Hero number
components.role: the anomaly promoted to 170 px black weight with a mono caption

components.name: Weight-ramp headline
components.role: tagline letters graded thin → heavy as a frozen wave

motion.name: Wave sweep
motion.how: wght 200 → 800 → 200 by distance from a moving front, 60 ms stagger per column, sine.inOut; crosses the grid in one bar (2 s at 120 BPM)

motion.name: Tension hold
motion.how: anomalies stay heavy and pulse 800 ↔ 700 every beat (500 ms) while everything else relaxes to 200

motion.name: Hero morph
motion.how: the anomaly scales 1 → 3.6 at weight 800, expo.out 800 ms, landing on the downbeat

story: Hook: a flat sea of numbers all at the same weight — '38 dashboards, everything looks equally important' — under 'How many dashboards did you check today?'. Reveal: a diagonal weight wave rolls across the grid on the drop and the lockup punches in at its peak, 'Acme' at 800, 'Pulse' at 200. Proof: the scan passes and everything thins back out except one glyph that holds at 800 in coral; it grows into '−18%' with 'Checkout conversion · since 09:42 · after deploy #2231', a wght legend explains the encoding, and the human hits Roll back. CTA: 'Every metric. Every minute.' as weight ramps, lockup and Start free.
adapt: Fill the grid with your own values (response times, stock levels, lead scores) and map deviation from normal to font weight; any variable font with a wide weight axis works.

fit.risk: subtle weight steps vanish after compression and at thumbnail size; use only ~200, ~500 and 800
